title: The Temperamental Nature of Alligator Gender-Reveal Parties - Nautilus
gist: A Journal of Experimental Biology study finds American alligator sex is set by just a one- or two-degree difference in incubation temperature, so warming could skew populations.

insights.claim: A study in the Journal of Experimental Biology found that the sex of American alligators (Alligator mississippiensis) is set by just a one- or two-degree difference in incubation temperature.
insights.so_what: Sensitive biological thresholds amplify climate-warming impacts on wildlife.
insights.quote: the sex of American alligators (Alligator mississippiensis) is set by just a one- or two-degree difference
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: With environmental temperatures rising, the narrow temperature threshold for alligator sex determination could produce lopsided alligator sex ratios.
insights.so_what: Example of second-order climate effects on species demographics.
insights.quote: With environmental temperatures on the upswing, that could make for lopsided alligator populations.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
